short: A return to hereditary succession that contemporaries blamed for ending the age of the adoptive emperors.
full:
Commodus was made co-emperor by his father Marcus Aurelius in 177 CE and became sole ruler on Marcus's death on 17 March 180 CE, promptly abandoning the Danube campaigns to make peace and return to Rome. Where his four adoptive predecessors had been chosen for competence, Commodus held office purely by birth, and ancient writers treated his reign as the moment the empire's fortunes turned.

He increasingly withdrew from administration in favour of court favourites, staged gladiatorial combats in which he fought personally, and had himself worshipped as a living Hercules. Repeated conspiracies against him culminated in his strangulation, arranged by his own chamberlain and mistress, on 31 December 192 CE. His death without an heir triggered a fresh succession crisis the following year.
